question_text:
Calculate the electrical conductivity of pure copper at (a) 400 °C and (b) –100 °C.  The resistivity of copper at 25 °C is 1.67×10⁻⁶ Ω·cm, and its temperature‐resistivity coefficient is α=0.0043 /°C. 


 Give your answers in S/cm as (σ₄₀₀, σ₋₁₀₀).The units of each required answer are (ohm^-1 \cdot cm^-1, ohm^-1 \cdot cm^-1), respectively.
response:
Using the linear resistivity–temperature relation

$$\rho(T)=\rho_{25}\bigl[1+\alpha(T-25)\bigr],\qquad \sigma=\frac{1}{\rho}$$

with $\rho_{25}=1.67\times10^{-6}\ \Omega\cdot\text{cm}$ and $\alpha=0.0043\ /^\circ\text{C}$:

**(a) At 400 °C**
$$\rho_{400}=1.67\times10^{-6}[1+0.0043(400-25)]=4.363\times10^{-6}\ \Omega\cdot\text{cm}$$
$$\sigma_{400}=\frac{1}{4.363\times10^{-6}}\approx2.29\times10^{5}\ \text{S/cm}$$

**(b) At –100 °C**
$$\rho_{-100}=1.67\times10^{-6}[1+0.0043(-100-25)]=7.724\times10^{-7}\ \Omega\cdot\text{cm}$$
$$\sigma_{-100}=\frac{1}{7.724\times10^{-7}}\approx1.29\times10^{6}\ \text{S/cm}$$

$$\boxed{(2.29\times10^{5},\ 1.29\times10^{6})}$$
